No, the legislature has the say in who the electors are.

The Constitution says “Each State shall appoint, in such Manner as the Legislature thereof may direct...” the choosing of the electors. Courts have pretty consistently held that directing the manner of choosing means that the process is run according to the laws the legislature has passed and in Arizona those laws state that the governor shall name a slate of electors (based on the certified popular vote total).

But here we’re talking about what happens if the legislature sends another slate of electors so that two batches of electoral votes from Arizona show up on December 14. That’s covered by the 1877 Electoral Count Act which says that the governor’s slate is the one that gets counted.

So I’m still not seeing how this is going to work.
